Geographies Served Programs Arogya Seva - Health for All (ASHA) Programme In its pursuit of Health for All (ASHA), the organisation facilitates free healthcare providers to become caring and cutting-edge service providers, aiming to save lives and enhance the quality of life for a vast number of people. It extends support for Telehealth Services, utilizing Health4All, a Free and Open Source Software developed by UC volunteers. These telehealth facilities include helpdesk services for Aakar Aasha Hospital, a reconstructive surgery centre, Raktadaan Helpline for blood donors, a hearing screening centre by Meenakshi Venkataraman Foundation, and a telehealth consultation helpline facilitated by Sri Sathya Sai Seva Organisations and Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Medical Sciences. With the assistance of over 100 volunteers, it provides Seva from Home to support these helplines and telehealth services. Preventive Healthcare Programme UC focuses on preventive healthcare by promoting health awareness and education at both personal and community levels, aiming to reduce the burden of diseases and associated costs. It is actively developing Health4All. Today, an interactive and multilingual platform that facilitates health education and encourages positive health choices. This content is utilized not only at health centres but also outside these facilities to reach a wider audience and promote healthier living. Healthcare for Remote Tribal Population Programme District Kothagudem State Telangana District Kothagudem States Telangana Since 2021, UC has been providing volunteer service support to the Indigenous Development Organisation (IDO), which focuses on enhancing maternal and child healthcare services in approximately 50 tribal hamlets located in the Bhadradri Kothagudem District of Telangana State. Palliative Care Services District Hyderabad Sri Sathya Sai State Andhra Pradesh Telangana District Hyderabad Sri Sathya Sai States Andhra Pradesh Telangana Addressing the universal need for Palliative Care and acknowledging its shortage, UC has been collaborating with the Pain Relief and Palliative Care Society (PRPCS) since June 2017. PRPCS strives to enhance the availability of Palliative Care services within the Public Health system and beyond. Operating a 30-bed capacity hospice for pediatric and adult patients in Hyderabad, PRPCS also provides support to around 500 patients through its home care program. In 2022, UC partnered with PRPCS to establish the Sri Sathya Sai Palliative Care Center in Puttaparthi, with the backing of the Alumni of Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Learning. Milestones & Track Record Facilitated various forms of philanthropy, including volunteering, in-kind donations, waste donations, and financial contributions, to drive result-oriented social work in healthcare, education, and the environment. --> --> Leadership Team P S Gunarajan Founder G Sathish Raju Board Member Shashi Mohan Kothari Board Member Gunaranjan P S Demographics & Structure Organisation Strength None M&E Internal, External Assessors No --> Political & Religious Declarations On Affiliation if any No On Deployment Bias if any No --> Registration Details PAN Card AABCU1456C Registration Number U93000AP2010NPL066991 CSR Form 1 Not Available VO ID / Darpan ID TS/2017/0179646 --> 80G AABCU1456CF20107 12A AABCU1456CE20109 FCRA 10231006 About Headquarters Hyderabad, Telangana Since 2009 Demographies Served Youth Women Children Men --> Impact UC's work generates resources for result-oriented social work, primarily in healthcare and also in education and environment, through collaboration with many NPOs and public institutions supported by institutional and individual donors.
